[{"address":"ms::p5::esc652","content":"{\"full_source_conversation\":\"supporter: Hello. How are you feeling today?\\nseeker: Hi, I'm feeling really anxious today.\\nsupporter: What has made you feel anxious?\\nseeker: Yesterday my company laid off 10% of the workforce and another 10% got furloughed.\\nseeker: I'm afraid I might be in the next round.\\nsupporter: I am very sorry to hear that. I am currently in a situation where furloughs are greatly affecting my family as well.\\nseeker: Oh no that's terrible.\\nseeker: The problem is, I am right now the only breadwinner in the family. My wife was laid off three months ago\\nsupporter: Are you given specifics on time of furlough?\\nseeker: No, it's basically until things get better.\\nsupporter: I know that's very difficult. And no doubt why you're here working for crumbs.\\nsupporter: It's why I'm here as well.\\nseeker: Yeah, trying to make ends meet wherever I can\\nseeker: I've been also trying to do uber as well but everyone is doing it also\\nsupporter: I know it's a difficult time. Yes Uber is definitely overrun right now. Have you taken any time out to address your anxiety so it doesn't become more serious? \\nseeker: I don't know what I can do. I've been trying to keep busy. And I can't afford a therapist or anything like that.\\nsupporter: Yes, that's definitely an expense you can't afford right now. But are you familiar with the concept of controlled breathing to help reduce or relieve anxiety?\\nseeker: Like meditation?\\nseeker: What am I supposed to do? Just breathe in and out a lot?\\nsupporter: Not exactly. Controlled breathing is more of getting yourself into a quiet room. Closing your eyes, and purposely and intently focusing on your breathing. Slowly breathe in for a count of 5, then slowly exhale for a count of 5. Repeat this process for approximately 10 minute. It will help your stress levels and help regulate your heart rate!\\nseeker: Oh I didn't know that. No, I haven't tried that. Does it really work?\\nsupporter: I've been using it myself over the past 3 months and it most definitely helps! But it's absolutely imperative to clear your mind and have complete quiet.\\nseeker: ok I can try it I guess\\nseeker: thanks for that tip\\nsupporter: No problem. I hope this gives you some relief! Stay strong!\\nseeker: yeah, thanks. same to you\\nsupporter: My final piece of advice would be to set aside time that is specified where nothing negative is discussed. No politics, no bills, nothing anxiety producing for you. It's probably best if this time is within an hour of your bedtime becuase anxiety is not conducive to a good night's sleep.\\nseeker: That's helpful. Thanks.\\nsupporter: No problem. Take care. Wishing you well on your situation.\\nseeker: Thanks. It must be really hard to see her go through this. How is she doing now?\\nseeker: She's stable now, thankfully. But every time she has an episode, it takes a toll on us, especially Margaret.\\nsupporter: I'm relieved to hear Emily is stable. The stress must be immense for you both. What's been the most difficult part?\\nseeker: I think it's the feeling of helplessness. We do everything we can, but it feels like we're just waiting for the next attack.\\nsupporter: That sounds overwhelming, Charles. Feeling helpless is tough. Have you found anything that helps ease that feeling, even a little?\\nseeker: Talking to someone helps a bit. And knowing we're following the doctor’s advice, but the uncertainty lingers.\\nsupporter: It's good that you're reaching out and following medical guidance. It's okay to feel uncertain; anyone would in your shoes.\\nseeker: Thanks, I appreciate that. Margaret tries to be strong for Emily, but I can see it's wearing her down too.\\nsupporter: Margaret sounds like a wonderful mother, but it's important for both of you to care for yourselves too. How are you supporting each other?\\nseeker: We're trying to talk things out and give each other breaks. It's a work in progress.\\nsupporter: That's a healthy approach. It's so important to lean on each other and take things one day at a time.\\nseeker: Yeah, some days are better than others. Getting back to a routine helps, but the worry is constant.\\nsupporter: That constant worry must be exhausting. Do you have any outlets or activities to help manage it?\\nseeker: I try to go for a run in the mornings. It's not much, but it clears my head for a bit.\\nsupporter: Exercise is great for stress relief. Even small moments of peace are valuable. You're doing your best, and that matters.\\nseeker: Thank you. It's good to hear that. It's just hard not to feel guilty for needing time away.\\nsupporter: Taking care of yourself isn't selfish; it's necessary. Being at your best helps you support Emily and Margaret even better.\\nseeker: You're right. I need to remember that. It's a delicate balance, but we're getting there.\\nsupporter: It sounds like you and Margaret are doing an incredible job under tough circumstances. Keep leaning on each other. You're not alone.\\nseeker: Thanks for listening. It really helps to talk things out and know someone understands.\\nsupporter: Anytime, Charles. I'm here whenever you need to talk.
